best_for: Windows and Mac users who want Drive inside Explorer or Finder, streaming to save disk space or mirroring to work offline.

points.title: Stream or mirror
points.text: Streaming keeps files in the cloud and needs an internet connection until a file has been opened. Mirroring keeps a full copy on your computer and in the cloud, so it is always available offline.

points.title: What can use which
points.text: Shared drives, other computers and USB backups can only be streamed. Local folders and the desktop can only be mirrored.

points.title: Storage still counts
points.text: Streamed files you own still count toward your Google storage, shared with Gmail and Photos. Mirrored files do not change your storage limit.

points.title: Up to four accounts
points.text: You can sign in with up to four accounts at once. Work and school accounts may be blocked, or an administrator must install it.

points.title: Windows requirements
points.text: 64-bit Windows 10 or later, Windows Server 2016 or later, or Windows 11 on Arm64. It needs Microsoft WebView2, which the installer adds when missing. 32-bit Windows is not supported.

points.title: macOS files live elsewhere
points.text: It needs macOS 13 or later, and on macOS 12.1 and up streamed files sit under ~/Library/CloudStorage, appearing in Finder's sidebar.

points.title: No Linux version
points.text: Google says the desktop app is not available on Linux; use Drive in the browser. It also does not support SMB or NFS network volumes or beta operating systems.
